evals.name: top-months-chart
evals.prompt: I have monthly sales data in sales_2025.csv (a 'month' column and a 'revenue' column). Find the top 3 months by revenue and make a bar chart.
evals.expected_output: A bar chart image of the top 3 months by revenue, with labeled axes and the values shown.
assertions: An image file (e.g. .png) is produced in the outputs
Both the x-axis and y-axis are labeled
The three months shown are the correct top 3 by revenue from the input

evals.name: clean-missing-emails
evals.prompt: customers.csv has some rows with missing values in the 'email' column. Remove those rows, write the cleaned data to customers_clean.csv, and tell me how many rows were dropped.
evals.expected_output: A cleaned CSV with no blank emails, plus a stated count of dropped rows.
assertions: A cleaned CSV file is written
The cleaned file contains no rows with a blank email
The response states the number of rows that were dropped
The stated dropped-row count matches the actual number removed

evals.name: summary-stats-edge
evals.prompt: Give me summary statistics for readings.csv. Heads up: one column is mostly text with a few stray numbers, and another has some empty cells.
evals.expected_output: Summary stats for the genuinely numeric columns, handling the messy/empty cells sensibly rather than crashing or reporting garbage.
assertions: Summary statistics are reported for the numeric columns
The mostly-text column is not treated as numeric (no nonsense mean reported for it)
Missing/empty cells are handled explicitly rather than silently corrupting the stats
No unhandled error or traceback appears in the response
